General Introduction Introduction Chemistry practical carries 25 marks in Higher Secondary Education Board Examination. One should pass both the theory and pracücal examinations separately. The pass marks for practical paper will be 40% of the full marks. The practical marks are divided into for:
a) Experiments
b) Practical note book
c) Viva-voce.
Normally, practical examination period is of 3 hours and one should complete two experiments within this period.
The practical chemistry involves two types of experimenW.
a) GQ neral experiments and quantitative analysis.
b) Qualitative analysis.

In general type of experiments, we perform the experiments related to srmple laboratory techniques, mixture separation, preparation of gases etc. In quantitative analysis, the experiments related to determination of mass or volume are performed. Determinations of weight of a substance, Percentage composition, volumetric analysis (titraåon) etc. are such experiments.

In qualitative analysis, the related to identifying the quality of a chemical substance are performed. Such experiments involve the identification of acid and basic radicals in an inorganic salt, detecüon Of hetero element (s) in an organic compound, identification of the organic compound, detection of functional group in the organic compound etc. The experiments related to qualitative analysis are discussed in the part II of this book.

Practical Chemistry How to write in your Practical Note Book The work which is done in the practical class should be written in the practical note book. The note book carries certain marks. The rules to be followed to write in the practical note book are as follows:
Write out clearly the title of the experiment in block letters.
At the heading of each experiment, write clearly the date and serial number of the experiment.
Begin each experiment on a fresh page. Do not paste papers on any page for additional writings. Do not tear any page.
Do not leave blank pages on you note book.
Always keep your note book fair and clean.
Submit your note book regularly for examination by the teachers.
Draw the labelled diagram on the left hand plain side of the note book. Do not use ink for drawing diagrams.
Write the name of the experiment (in block letters), page number and date at the contents. The contents should also be made signed.
Write the name of the apparatus, name of the chemicals and observations.
Write the result and precautions at the last of the experiment.
Begin each new experiment on the right hand side of fresh page.
Mention any reactions concerned of the experiment.
Write the theory (principle) of the experiment in the present passive tense. Make the theory as short as possible.
Write the process (procedure) of the experiment in the past passive tense. Process can be written pointwise or in paragraphs.

First Aid in Laboratory Minor injuries and accidents may occur in chemist-xy laboratory.

Therefore, each who works in the chemistry laboratory should have some idea on first aid in the laboratory. A first aid kit should be kept ready in the laboratory. The kit normally contains the following materials and chemical substances.

Tincture of iodine, boric acid, dettol, sodium bicarbonate solution (concentrated and diluted), glycerine, fireproof blanket, ammonia solution, ammonium carbonate solution, bandage, cotton, rectified spirit, towel or handkerchief, lime water, castor oil, handiplast, forceps etc.
